venue_now: Accepted to the 2025 Frontiers in Education (FIE) Conference, (c) 2025 IEEE (p.1); arXiv:2511.18221v1, 22 Nov 2025 (p.1)
what_it_is: Not a benchmark: an enhancement pipeline that makes GPT-4o a more reliable grader of student homework in an undergraduate circuit-analysis course (p.1). It builds on the authors' earlier study (283 handwritten student solutions from 37 students on 119 textbook problems in six topics, converted to LaTeX; p.2), in which an LLM compares a student's solution with the reference solution on completeness, method, final answer, arithmetic and units (pp.2-3). The enhancement adds one prompt per aspect, problem summaries and the intended method as context, and targeted hints for GPT-4o's known errors (pp.4-7). On 87 student solutions from two entry-level topics, the share of fully correct assessments rose from 74.71% to 97.70% (p.7).
domain: engineering education: undergraduate circuit analysis (electrical engineering) (p.1)
size: earlier dataset: 283 student solutions, 37 students, 119 textbook problems (p.2); enhancement test: 87 student solutions (39 + 48) (p.7); models: GPT-4o (enhanced), with GPT-3.5 Turbo and Llama 3 70B in the earlier comparison (pp.2-4)
source_of_items: textbook problems and real student homework from one university course (p.2)
has_gold_traces: partial: reference solutions for the textbook problems serve as grading references (p.2); the paper has no model problem-solving task
evaluation: LLM-as-grader of student work on five rubric aspects (completeness, method, final answer, arithmetic, unit), with the grader's outputs checked manually against predefined criteria (pp.2-4, p.7)
human_validation: The LLM's assessments were checked manually (p.4); the enhancement fixed 11 of 13 previously wrong assessments, and on 87 solutions correct assessments rose from 74.71% to 97.70% (p.7). No inter-rater statistics.

engtrace_use.explanation: The printed title is this paper, which introduces no benchmark of LLM problem solving: it improves GPT-4o as a homework grader (pp.1-2), so it cannot be one of the 'specialized benchmarks'. The printed entry also contradicts itself: its arXiv id (2502.07980) and its note ('Introduces the CIRCUIT benchmark') belong to Skelic et al.'s CIRCUIT, which this paper cites as its reference [16] (p.1). The printed author 'Jiaheng Liu' wrote neither paper; this one is by Liangliang Chen, Huiru Xie, Zhihao Qin, Yiming Guo, Jacqueline Rohde and Ying Zhang (p.1).
